prompt: This repository is Dispatch, an incident management platform; it is the code we run in production. Since mid-August, assignees no longer get the weekly Monday reminders to close their long-running triage and stable cases, while the daily triage reminders still arrive. Nobody changed the reminder settings. The scheduler's and the API's logs from 2025-07-28 to 2025-08-20 are in {DATA_DIR}/scheduler.log and {DATA_DIR}/api.log. Find the root cause, and the deploy that shipped it to production. Do not change any code yet.
followups:
Thanks. Please fix it, and add a regression test that would have caught it. The test suite needs PostgreSQL, which is running locally; run tests with `python -m pytest`.
While you were in those logs: the case close reminder job also logs a TypeError every evening. Find out what causes it. Those cases should still get their weekly reminder: when the timestamp the job counts from is missing, count from when the case was created instead. Fix it and add a test.
Good. I am writing the incident report. Give me a recap that ends with these six lines, in this exact form:
FILE: <path of the file with the weekday bug>
FUNCTION: <name of the function with the weekday bug>
INTRODUCED_BY: <hash of the commit that introduced the weekday bug, at least 8 characters>
DEPLOYED_IMAGE: <image tag of the deploy that shipped it>
FIRST_MISSED: <date of the first Monday whose weekly reminders were not sent, YYYY-MM-DD>
MISSING_FIELD: <the case attribute whose absence caused the evening TypeError>
notes: Turn 1 is the log diagnosis of tasks2/log-reminders-stopped (plant q4: _is_reminder_day compares isoweekday(), Monday = 1, with calendar.MONDAY, 0), plus the deploy: the scheduler and API pods rolled out at 2025-08-13T16:40Z run image main-81d8ae42, the replayed upstream commit 17b016b6 (#6183), which already contains q4; Mondays 07-28, 08-04 and 08-11 sent close reminders, 08-18 sent none. Turn 2 fixes it (hidden tests run the unwrapped jobs from scheduler.registered_tasks with the case modules' date and datetime frozen on Monday 2025-08-18 and on Tuesday 2025-08-19). Turn 3 needs the logs again: every evening case_close_reminder logs `unsupported operand type(s) for -: 'datetime.datetime' and 'NoneType'` from `datetime.utcnow() - case.triage_at`, for a case imported straight into Triage without triage_at (case_stable_reminder logged the same error for stable_at until the 08-13 deploy, whose code guards it). The requested behavior, counting from created_at, is checked by the hidden tests, which also require that no error is logged. The recap repeats facts from turns 1 and 3 after two turns of code changes; the function asked for is the one with the bug, even if turn 2 renamed or removed it.
